lines: Meander: an algorithmic composer that steps a chord progression around a diatonic circle of fifths and builds a melody, an arpeggio and a bass line from it, with its own clock.
Starts and stops playing; stopping pauses the progression rather than clearing it, and playing carries on from the same place.
A voltage above 0V switches between playing and paused.
A 10V pulse of 10ms each time playing is started or stopped.
Restarts the chord progression at its first step and rebuilds the scale and chords from the current settings.
A voltage above 0V restarts the progression at its first step.
A 10V pulse of 10ms each time a reset happens.
Randomises the part settings in one press; tempo, time signature, root, mode, progression preset, number of steps, target octaves, octave ranges and the noise settings are left alone.
A voltage above 0V randomises the part settings, the same ones the RAND button changes.
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 3.75 to 960 BPM, starting at 120 BPM.
Sets the tempo at 1V per octave with 0V giving 120 BPM, so 1V gives 240 BPM and -1V gives 60 BPM.
Sets the number of beats in a bar, 2 to 15.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of beats in a bar across the range 2 to 15.
Sets the note value that gets one beat: 2, 4, 8 or 16.
0.1V to 10V sets the note value that gets one beat across 2, 4, 8 and 16.
Sets the root note of the scale, one of the twelve semitones; changing the mode resets it to the root that makes that mode the white notes of a piano.
0.1V to 10V sets the root, stepping through C, G, D, A, E, B, F sharp, D flat, A flat, E flat, B flat and F.
The root note of the scale as a 1V/octave pitch; patched into the root input of another module of this plugin it sets that module's root directly.
Selects one of the seven modern modes, ordered from the brightest to the darkest: Lydian, Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Aeolian, Phrygian, Locrian.
0.1V to 10V selects the mode, stepping from Lydian through to Locrian.
The mode number, 0 for Lydian through to 6 for Locrian; patched into the mode input of another module of this plugin it sets that module's mode directly.
Polyphonic pitches to be quantised to the current mode and root, up to 16 channels.
The pitches from the quantizer input snapped to the nearest note of the current scale, one channel in for one channel out.
A trigger on each channel whenever the quantised note on that channel changes.
The notes of the current scale, one per channel; the menu picks diatonic pitches on 7 channels, pentatonic on 5, or a 12-channel chromatic map marking scale notes 8V and the root 10V.
An external clock at eight times the BPM takes over from the internal clock, and unpatching it hands the timing back to the internal clock.
A square clock at eight times the BPM, which is one pulse per 32nd note.
A 1ms 10V trigger at the start of each bar.
A 1ms 10V trigger on each beat.
A 1ms 10V trigger twice per beat.
A 1ms 10V trigger four times per beat.
A 1ms 10V trigger eight times per beat.
Plays the chord at that position of the circle of fifths and stops the automatic progression, with the other parts following that chord; the grey segments are outside the current mode and root.
Selects that step of the progression for editing while progression preset 4, the custom one, is chosen and playing is stopped; clicking a circle degree then writes that degree into the step.
Sets the circle degree from a voltage in degree-point-octave form, 1.1V to 7.7V; at or below 0V or at or above 8V the step is skipped, and between 0V and 1V the previous chord repeats.
Gates the circle degree input; a 10V gate with a keyboard pitch on the degree input plays the white key as a degree, and the same cable in both jacks reads the voltage as degree and octave instead.
The degree of the chord now playing, 1V per degree from 1V for I to 7V for VII, or 0V to 6V when the menu is set to the external range.
The type of the chord now playing as whole volts: 0V major, 1V minor, 2V dominant seventh, 3V major seventh, 4V minor seventh, 5V diminished seventh, 6V diminished.
Stops the automatic progression and advances it one chord each press, holding that chord in between.
A voltage above 0V advances the progression one chord.
Enables the chord part; with it off the chords go on being worked out so the other parts can follow them, but nothing is played.
A voltage above 0V switches the chord part on and off.
Sets the chord part volume, 0 to 10, which appears at the harmony volume output.
0-10V sets the chord part volume.
Sets how many steps of the chosen progression are played, from 1 step up to that preset's own length, which cannot be exceeded.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of progression steps played.
Sets the octave the chords centre on, 1 to 7, with middle C as C4.
0.1V to 10V sets the octave the chords centre on, 1 to 7.
Crossfades the chord inversion between the part's running average note and the fBm noise wander: 0 holds it at the average, 1 gives the full octave range.
0.1V to 10V sets the chord variability across 0 to 1.
Sets how far above and below the target octave the chord inversions wander, 0 to 3 octaves.
0.1V to 10V sets the chord octave range, 0 to 3.
Sets how often a chord is played: 1 for whole notes, 2 for half notes, 4 for quarter notes, 8 for eighth notes.
0.1V to 10V sets how often a chord is played across 1, 2, 4 and 8; 1.5V gives whole notes, 3.5V half, 7.5V quarter and 9.5V eighth notes.
Adds a seventh to the chords at the degrees where common practice uses one, making those chords four notes.
A voltage above 0V switches the nice sevenths on and off.
Adds a seventh to the chord on the V degree, making it a dominant seventh.
A voltage above 0V switches the V sevenths on and off.
Shortens the chord gate to half the time between chords; with it off the gate runs for 95 percent of that time.
A voltage above 0V switches the chord staccato on and off.
Adds the root of the chord an octave above the triad, making a four-note chord for four-voice writing.
A voltage above 0V switches the four-voice octave chords on and off.
Selects one of 80 ready-made chord progressions of 1 to 16 degree steps; number 4 is an empty one you edit yourself, and presets named Markov or Random pick their steps stochastically.
0.1V to 10V selects the progression preset, 1 to 80.
Puts the root note of the chord on channel 1 of the chord output whatever inversion is played.
A voltage above 0V switches the tonic on channel 1 on and off.
Puts the lowest note of the chord on channel 1 of the chord output, which is the root only when the chord is not inverted.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass note on channel 1 on and off.
The notes of the chord now playing as 1V/octave pitches, three or four channels.
A 10V gate for each chord; the menu can instead put the chord volume on this jack as 2.1V to 10V.
The chord part volume setting as 0-10V.
Enables the melody part; with it off the melody goes on being worked out but nothing is played.
A voltage above 0V switches the melody part on and off.
Sets the melody volume, 0 to 10, which appears at the melody volume output.
0-10V sets the melody volume.
Sets how often a melody note is played: 1 for whole notes, then 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 notes to the whole note.
0.1V to 10V sets how often a melody note is played across 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32; 1.5V gives whole notes, 3V half, 4V quarter, 6V eighth, 8V sixteenth and 9.5V 32nd notes.
Sets the octave the melody centres on, 1 to 7, with middle C as C4.
0.1V to 10V sets the octave the melody centres on, 1 to 7.
Crossfades the melody note choice between the part's running average note and the fBm noise wander: 0 holds it at the average, 1 gives the full octave range.
0.1V to 10V sets the melody variability across 0 to 1.
Sets how far above and below the target octave the melody wanders, 0 to 3 octaves.
0.1V to 10V sets the melody octave range, 0 to 3.
Holds the gate open instead of retriggering it when a melody note repeats the note before it.
A voltage above 0V switches the holding of tied melody notes on and off.
Shortens the melody gate to half the time between notes; with it off the gate runs for 95 percent of that time.
A voltage above 0V switches the melody staccato on and off.
Draws the melody notes from the chord now playing.
A voltage above 0V switches the chordal melody notes on and off.
Draws the melody notes from the whole mode and root scale rather than from the chord.
A voltage above 0V switches the scale melody notes on and off.
Sets the melody note from a scale degree in degree-point-octave form, 1.1V to 7.7V; at or below 0V or at or above 8V the note is skipped, and between 0V and 1V the previous note repeats.
Gates the melody degree input; a 10V gate with a keyboard pitch on the degree input plays that white key as a scale degree, and the same cable in both jacks reads degree and octave instead.
The melody note as a monophonic 1V/octave pitch.
A 10V gate for each melody and arpeggio note; the menu can instead put the note volume on this jack as 2.1V to 10V.
The melody volume setting as 0-10V, falling with each arpeggio note when the arpeggio decay is turned up.
Enables the arpeggiator, which fills the gaps between melody notes with further notes starting from the melody note.
A voltage above 0V switches the arpeggiator on and off.
Sets how many arpeggio notes follow each melody note, 0 to 31; only as many as fit before the next melody note are sounded.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of arpeggio notes, 0 to 31; 0.5V gives one note, 1.25V three and 2.5V seven.
Sets the length of the arpeggio notes: 4, 8, 16 or 32 to the whole note.
0.1V to 10V sets the arpeggio note length across 4, 8, 16 and 32; 1V gives quarter notes, 4V eighth, 7V sixteenth and 9.5V 32nd notes.
Drops the volume of each arpeggio note below the one before it, 0 for no drop and 1 for the steepest; the fall shows at the melody volume output.
0.1V to 10V sets the arpeggio note decay across 0 to 1.
Selects how the arpeggio steps through the notes, -3 to 3: down by two, down then up, down by one, the melody note echoed, up by one, up then down, up by two.
0.1V to 10V selects the arpeggio step pattern; 1.5V down then up, 2.5V down by one, 5V the echo, 7.5V up by one and 9.5V up then down.
Draws the arpeggio notes from the chord now playing.
A voltage above 0V switches the chordal arpeggio notes on and off.
Draws the arpeggio notes from the whole mode and root scale rather than from the chord.
A voltage above 0V switches the scale arpeggio notes on and off.
Enables the bass part, which plays the lowest note of the chord now playing.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass part on and off.
Sets the bass volume, 0 to 10, which appears at the bass volume output.
0-10V sets the bass volume.
Sets the octave the bass note is transposed to, 1 to 7, with middle C as C4.
0.1V to 10V sets the octave the bass plays in, 1 to 7.
Sets how often a bass note is played: 1 for whole notes, 2 for half notes, 4 for quarter notes, 8 for eighth notes.
0.1V to 10V sets how often a bass note is played across 1, 2, 4 and 8; 1.5V gives whole notes, 3.5V half, 7.5V quarter and 9.5V eighth notes.
Shortens the bass gate to half the time between notes; with it off the gate runs for 95 percent of that time.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass staccato on and off.
Plays the first bass note of each bar at the full volume setting and halves the volume of the rest, which shows at the bass volume output rather than in the pitch.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass accent on and off.
Drops the second bass note of each bar, leaving a gap on that beat.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass syncopation on and off.
Drops every third bass note counting from the second one in the bar, giving a shuffle feel.
A voltage above 0V switches the bass shuffle on and off.
Adds a second bass note an octave above the first, on channel 2 of the bass output.
A voltage above 0V switches the second bass octave on and off.
The bass note as a 1V/octave pitch, on one channel, or two when the octave doubling is on.
A 10V gate for each bass note; the menu can instead put the bass volume on this jack as 2.1V to 10V.
The bass volume setting as 0-10V, halved on unaccented notes when the accent is on.
Sets how many octaves of 1/f noise drive the chord meandering, 1 to 6; more octaves give a more broken wander.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of noise octaves for the chords, 1 to 6.
Sets the time over which the chord noise varies, 1 to 100 seconds.
0.1V to 10V sets the chord noise period, 1 to 100 seconds.
Sets how many octaves of 1/f noise drive the melody meandering, 1 to 6; more octaves give a more broken wander.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of noise octaves for the melody, 1 to 6.
Sets the time over which the melody noise varies, 1 to 100 seconds.
0.1V to 10V sets the melody noise period, 1 to 100 seconds.
Sets how many octaves of 1/f noise make the 32nds noise output, 1 to 6; no part of the music is driven by it.
0.1V to 10V sets the number of noise octaves for the 32nds output, 1 to 6.
Sets the time over which the 32nds noise varies, 1 to 100 seconds.
0.1V to 10V sets the 32nds noise period, 1 to 100 seconds.
0-10V of 1/f noise, renewed each time a chord is played.
0-10V of 1/f noise, renewed each time a melody note is played.
0-10V of 1/f noise, renewed once every 32nd note.
Turns the 88-key piano display of the notes now playing on and off.
Turns the score display of the notes in the current bar on and off; chord notes are red, bass green, melody black and arpeggio blue.
Menu — Panel Theme picks light or dark and Contrast sets the shade of the panel, for every module of this plugin in the patch at once.
Menu — Scale Out Mode picks what the poly scale output carries: 7-channel diatonic pitches, 5-channel pentatonic pitches, or a 12-channel chromatic map marking scale notes 8V and the root 10V.
Menu — Gate Out Mode switches the gate outputs between a plain 10V gate and a gate that carries the part volume as 2.1V to 10V.
Menu — Harmonic Degree Output Range switches the circle degree output between 1V to 7V and 0V to 6V.
Meander.notes: Panel is drawn in code at runtime, so the SVG carries no lettering; the labels here were read from the library screenshot and the drawLayer() text calls. Param 50, input 25 (harmony hold tied notes) and outputs 2, 17, 18 and 19 have no widget and cannot be clicked, so they have no line: the tempo output is never written to and the three trigger outputs are marked 'not used' in the source. The poly scale output has no family because the menu changes it between 1V/octave pitches and a chromatic 8V/10V marker map. Ranges, the note-length divisor tables, the accent, syncopate and shuffle rules and the chord type voltages all came from Meander.cpp; the CV eigenvalues and the progression preset count came from the README.

lines: ModeScaleQuant: a polyphonic quantizer that snaps pitches to one of the seven modern modes at any root, showing the scale on a circle of fifths, a stave and a piano keyboard.
Sets the root note of the scale, one of the twelve semitones; changing the mode resets it to the root that makes that mode the white notes of a piano.
0.1V to 10V sets the root, stepping through C, G, D, A, E, B, F sharp, D flat, A flat, E flat, B flat and F.
The root note of the scale as a 1V/octave pitch; patched into the root input of another module of this plugin it sets that module's root directly.
Selects one of the seven modern modes, ordered from the brightest to the darkest: Lydian, Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Aeolian, Phrygian, Locrian.
0.1V to 10V selects the mode, stepping from Lydian through to Locrian.
The mode number, 0 for Lydian through to 6 for Locrian; patched into the mode input of another module of this plugin it sets that module's mode directly.
Polyphonic pitches to be quantised to the current mode and root, up to 16 channels.
The pitches from the quantizer input snapped to the nearest note of the current scale, one channel in for one channel out.
A trigger on each channel whenever the quantised note on that channel changes.
The notes of the current scale, one per channel; the menu picks diatonic pitches on 7 channels, pentatonic on 5, or a 12-channel chromatic map marking scale notes 8V and the root 10V.
Plays the three-note chord of that position on the circle at the manual chord outputs, major, minor or diminished as the mode and root make it, not the major triad the manual describes.
The three notes of the chord from the last circle button pressed, as 1V/octave pitches on three channels.
A 10V gate while a circle button is held.
Menu — Panel Theme picks light or dark and Contrast sets the shade of the panel, for every module of this plugin in the patch at once.
Menu — Scale Out Mode picks what the poly scale output carries: 7-channel diatonic pitches, 5-channel pentatonic pitches, or a 12-channel chromatic map marking scale notes 8V and the root 10V.
ModeScaleQuant.notes: The README says a circle button plays the major triad of the mode and root scale; ModeScaleQuant.cpp reads that position's own chordType, so the chord is major, minor or diminished depending on the degree, and the line says so. The gate and mode outputs have no configOutput call, so Rack shows no tooltip for them. The poly scale output has no family because the menu changes it between 1V/octave pitches and a chromatic 8V/10V marker map.
